result.label: bug
result.what_to_change: parseAmount's symbol-stripping regex (`/[\s€$£¥]/g`) only recognizes a hardcoded list of currency symbols and doesn't include ₹ (rupee) or handle multi-character prefixes like "CHF" or apostrophe thousands separators (e.g. CHF 1'200.00); it should strip a broader/currency-aware set of symbols (or use the row's currency to know what prefix/format to expect) instead of a narrow hardcoded character class.
result.evidence: parseAmount in src/util/money.ts does `raw.replace(/[\s€$£¥]/g, "")` before validating with `/^\d+(\.\d+)?$/`; since ₹ is not in that character class, an amount like ₹1,250.00 keeps the ₹ character and fails the regex test, returning null, which schema.ts turns into the 'errors.badAmount' ("The amount is not a number") error reported in the issue. The same narrow symbol list also explains the reported CHF 1'200.00 failure (CHF prefix and apostrophe separator aren't stripped either).

not_searched: src/ingest/parser.ts (how RawRow is produced, in case symbol stripping belongs there instead)

input.title: Broaden currency symbol stripping in parseAmount
input.body:
File: src/util/money.ts

parseAmount's symbol-stripping regex (/[\s€$£¥]/g) only covers a hardcoded list of currency symbols, so it misses ₹ and multi-character prefixes like "CHF" or apostrophe thousands separators (e.g. CHF 1'200.00). Update it to strip a broader/currency-aware set of symbols, or use the row's currency to know what prefix/format to expect, before validating the numeric string.
